subject.summary: M31, the Andromeda Galaxy: a barred spiral of about a trillion stars 2.5 million light-years away, seen at its measured 77-degree inclination, with its bulge, its near-side dust lanes, the 10 kpc star-forming ring, and the companions M32 and M110.

facts.note: Tilted 77 degrees relative to Earth's view; 90 would be edge-on.
D25 isophotal diameter, 46.56 kpc (RC3). Modelled as 152 scene units of 1 kly.
A thin stellar disc; the model's drawn thickness, slightly generous so it reads.
The box/peanut bulge extends to 3.2 kpc in the disc plane (10.4 kly).
Star-forming ring of radius 9.8 kpc (32 kly), fitted as a circle offset from the nucleus.
Two logarithmic spirals with pitch angles of 9 and 9.5 degrees.
The two spirals are phase-shifted by 166 degrees.
The arms are not continuous but composed of spiral segments.
The north-west half of the disc is nearest to us; the dust is silhouetted there.
Projected separation from the nucleus: 24 arcmin at 2.5 Mly.
About 8.7 by 6.5 arcmin, traced from the reference image.
21.9 by 11.0 arcmin, traced from the reference image.
The radius drawn; M31's stellar halo is known to reach about 1.3 Mly.
Scene units are metres by contract; this construct is a scale model at 1 m = 1 kly.

parts.label: Stellar halo and globular clusters
parts.note: Halo stars and globular clusters; drawn far flatter and smaller than the real 1.3 Mly halo.

parts.label: Dust lane (near side)
parts.note: Silhouetted against the bulge: the near side is the north-west half of the disc.

parts.label: M32 (NGC 221)
parts.note: Compact elliptical companion (dE2), in front of the disc.

parts.label: M110 (NGC 205)
parts.note: Larger, fainter elliptical (dE6) beyond the disc, with its own dust patches.

identity.feature: A thin disc at 77 degrees inclination, about four times longer than it is tall
A bright central bulge with a compact nucleus, fatter than the disc
Dark dust lanes silhouetted on the near side, crossing the face of the bulge
Two tightly wound spiral arms, broken into segments, with blue star clouds
The offset 10 kpc ring of star formation
Two bright companions: compact M32 in front of the disc, large faint M110 beyond it
